query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics (AIMD) thermodynamic-integration workflows with an actively learned, phase-spanning equivariant machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) as the sampling Hamiltonian, followed by low-variance multistate free-energy reweighting from MLIP to the target DFT (Mermin finite-T) Hamiltonian for both solid and liquid, will deliver DFT-fidelity fusion free energies and high-temperature thermodynamics of multicomponent alloys at ≥100× lower CPU cost than AIMD-based free-energy methods and ≥5–10× lower cost than TOR-TILD in quaternary–quinary systems, while retaining vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
generation.material_initial_state: Chemically disordered concentrated alloy (3–5 transition-metal components) represented by SQS-like supercells for the solid (appropriate crystal prototype, e.g., fcc or bcc) and an equilibrated liquid at the same composition; system sizes ≥200 atoms to suppress finite-size bias.
generation.intervention: Use an actively learned equivariant ML potential (e.g., NequIP/ACE-like) trained on a joint set of solid and liquid configurations spanning 0.7–1.2× the melting range. Compute solid and liquid free energies with cheap ML-MD via reference-coupling TI (Einstein-crystal for solid; WCA or soft-core reference for liquid), then correct to DFT via single-step free-energy perturbation/MBAR reweighting using a modest number (O(10^2)) of DFT single-point Mermin free energies evaluated on ML-MD snapshots at each T. Enforce overlap diagnostics (effective sample size, variance of ΔU, KL divergence) and add active-learning queries if diagnostics fail.
generation.conditions:
- DFT functional fixed across all methods; Mermin finite-temperature DFT with electronic smearing matching target T for electron–vibration coupling.
- Temperatures: 0.6–1.3× estimated Tm; pressures: 0–5 GPa; supercells ≥200 atoms (liquid) and ≥256 atoms (solid) with appropriate SQS disorder.
- ML-MD: timesteps ~1 fs, trajectories ≥200 ps per T per phase for statistics; TI paths with ≥8–12 λ points and Gauss–Legendre integration.
- Reweighting: per T and phase, evaluate 64–256 DFT single-point free energies (energies + Mermin electronic term) on decorrelated ML-MD snapshots; use MBAR across neighboring T to increase overlap and reduce variance.
generation.structural_mediator: High configurational and energetic overlap between MLIP- and DFT-sampled ensembles across both phases, quantified by: (i) small variance of ΔU = U_DFT − U_ML (σ[ΔU] ≲ 20 meV/atom), (ii) MBAR effective sample size Neff ≥ 50 per phase per T, (iii) KL divergence between ML and DFT energy distributions D_KL ≤ 0.2. Structural distributions (pair distribution functions, angular distributions, and vibrational DOS) reproduced by MLIP within statistical error of AIMD baselines.
generation.mechanism: The MLIP captures anharmonic vibrational and liquid structural fluctuations at near-DFT fidelity but at classical-MD cost; free-energy perturbation/MBAR corrects the small residual free-energy gap between MLIP and DFT. Using Mermin finite-T DFT for single-point corrections retains electron–vibration coupling. Because the reference (MLIP) closely approximates the target Hamiltonian in both phases, the reweighting has low variance and requires only O(10^2) DFT evaluations, independent of trajectory length or system size, yielding large speedups.
generation.predicted_outcome:
- Throughput: ≥100× CPU-hour reduction vs explicit AIMD TI/coexistence for fusion free energies and melting points in quinary alloys; ≥5–10× vs TOR-TILD at the same DFT level for multicomponent systems.
- Fidelity: Per-atom Helmholtz/Gibbs free energies within 3–10 meV/atom of AIMD baselines over 0.7–1.2×Tm; melting temperature within 1–3% (typically ≤50 K for 1500–2500 K systems); entropy and latent heat of fusion within 5–10%; Cp(T) in solid and liquid within 5% above 0.7×Tm.
- Scaling: Cost grows weakly with component count once the MLIP descriptor embeds species, maintaining overlap so that DFT correction cost remains roughly constant per T and phase.
generation.baseline: Converged ab initio MD free-energy workflows using the same DFT functional: (i) direct TI to DFT from harmonic and liquid references or (ii) two-phase coexistence for Tm determination; and TOR-TILD where available, all at matched supercell sizes and k-point/electronic-temperature settings.
generation.boundary:
- Composition: Concentrated random solutions of 3–5 transition metals without strong localized f-electron physics or large charge-transfer/ionicity; moderate magnetism without sharp magnetic-order transitions near Tm.
- Temperature: 0.6–1.3× Tm; above this range, electronic excitations beyond Mermin DFT or incipient vaporization may degrade fidelity.
- Methodological: Reweighting applicability requires overlap diagnostics (σ[ΔU], Neff, D_KL) to pass; if they fail, additional active learning or broader training data is required. Highly directional/covalent melts or systems with liquid–liquid transitions may violate assumptions.
generation.uncertainty: Primary risks are (i) insufficient ensemble overlap in chemically extreme HEAs or at very high T, leading to biased reweighting; (ii) MLIP transferability gaps across rarely sampled chemical motifs; (iii) residual nonadiabatic electron–ion effects not captured by Mermin DFT; and (iv) hidden finite-size effects in liquids. The predicted speedups and error bounds may weaken for systems with strong magneto-structural fluctuations or significant short-range order changes between solid and liquid.

falsification_experiment.design: Select three multicomponent alloys (one quaternary, two quinary) spanning fcc and bcc solid solutions. For each: (1) Train an active-learning equivariant MLIP on joint solid–liquid data from 0.7–1.2× estimated Tm. (2) Compute MLIP free energies F_s^ML(T), F_l^ML(T) via TI from Einstein/WCA references. (3) Compute DFT corrections ΔF_s(T), ΔF_l(T) by MBAR/perturbation using 64–256 DFT Mermin free-energy single points per phase per T on ML-MD snapshots, verifying overlap diagnostics. (4) Obtain DFT-level free energies F_s/l^DFT≈F_s/l^ML+ΔF and Tm from equal-Gibbs/free-energy crossing; derive ΔS_fus, L_fus, Cp(T). (5) Independently compute baselines with explicit AIMD TI or two-phase coexistence (and TOR-TILD if available) using identical DFT settings. Compare costs and results.
measurements: Per-atom Helmholtz/Gibbs free energies F_s(T), F_l(T) over 0.7–1.2×Tm
Melting temperature Tm (equal-G or coexistence) at specified pressure
Entropy and latent heat of fusion (ΔS_fus, L_fus)
Heat capacity Cp(T) in solid and liquid
Ensemble-overlap diagnostics: σ[ΔU], Neff, D_KL for reweighting
Total CPU hours for each workflow normalized by supercell size and T-grid
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, for any tested alloy with overlap diagnostics satisfied (σ[ΔU] ≤ 20 meV/atom, Neff ≥ 50, D_KL ≤ 0.2), either (a) the per-atom phase free energies deviate by >10 meV/atom from the AIMD baseline over any 0.7–1.2×Tm interval or the predicted Tm differs by >3% (or >50 K) from baseline, or (b) the end-to-end CPU-hour cost reduction is <10× versus AIMD and <5× versus TOR-TILD at matched accuracy.
